free_tier.stated: USD 200 in free credits with no credit card required, described as 'Enough for ~4,000 hours of basic usage'. No feature gates: 'Unlimited sandboxes', 'All pre-built templates'.
free_tier.notes: A one-time balance spent per second. No reset and no expiry date is published. The terms page states credits 'may expire under posted program rules' without posting a rule.

per_object_cap.stated: Resources are set by the template, not the caller: 'Resources (vcpu, memory, disk) are always loaded from the template. You cannot specify custom resources when creating a sandbox.' A custom template can be built at 'CPU: 1-64 cores, Memory: 512MB-64GB, Disk: 1GB-250GB'.
per_object_cap.notes: the per-sandbox maximum is whatever the platform accepts on a template build; the range above is labelled 'Typical ranges' and 'depend on your plan', so it is not a published hard cap

retention.stated: A sandbox is destroyed when its timeout expires, and 'All data in the sandbox is lost'; pause and resume preserve state, and a stopped sandbox keeps its filesystem. No retention period for a stopped sandbox is published.

egress.terms: No egress charge or allowance is published on the pricing page; the page prices compute, memory and storage only.

limits.value: rate card USD 0.000014 per vCPU-second, USD 0.0000045 per GiB-second, USD 0.00000003 per GiB-second of storage
shape fixed by template; a template build accepts 1-64 cores, 512MB-64GB RAM, 1-250GB disk
a sandbox is destroyed when its timeout expires; the default is no timeout and the ceiling is not published

limits_note: Every sandbox can carry a timeout and is destroyed when it expires. The SDK signature gives timeout_seconds a default of 'no timeout', the docs illustrate 5 minutes to 4 hours, and the marketing page claims 'Up to 30 days runtime'. No page states a maximum, so whether a 730-hour timeout is accepted is undocumented.

identity_cost.detail: The pricing page states 'No credit card required' and '$200 free credits'; no card, no phone and no ID are mentioned. IMPORTANT: the console at console.hopx.ai (and console.hopx.dev, which the docs link to) offers ONLY 'Connect to HopX with: Google GitHub' — a browser OAuth button pair, with no email-and-password field anywhere on the page. The account is therefore created by an OAuth identity, not by an email form. No hold exists because no payment method is taken.

reliability_note: The pricing page's own worked example prices a 1 vCPU / 1 GiB / 10 GiB hour at '$0.05', while its rate card gives USD 0.06768 for the same hour, a 26% understatement.
confidence_note: Credit, the three unit rates, the OAuth-only console, the template-bound resources and the timeout semantics were each read on a first-party page. The maximum shape and the maximum timeout are not published.

notes: Arithmetic, recomputed today: 1 vCPU x USD 0.0504 + 1 GiB x USD 0.0162 + 10 GiB x USD 0.00108 = USD 0.06768 an hour. USD 200 / 0.06768 = 2,955.1 h = 123.1 days of a 1 vCPU / 1 GiB / 10 GiB box at 24/7, and a 730-hour month costs USD 49.41. The vendor's '~4,000 hours' headline counts the vCPU rate only and is 35% optimistic against its own rate card; the record uses the rate card. The vendor's own worked example also understates the same hour at '$0.05' against USD 0.06768. This is the most hours per no-card dollar of the three by a factor of four over E2B and of two and a half over Daytona at its max shape, but the box is 1 vCPU against Daytona's 4, so it is not a faster machine, only a longer-lived one. GPU trap: none to check, because no GPU product is advertised on the pricing page; the rate card is CPU only. The real caveat is identity: the console offers Google and GitHub OAuth ONLY, with no email form, so the account is tied to a Google or GitHub identity rather than an email address. Not published anywhere: the maximum template shape, the maximum timeout, the credit expiry, and any egress allowance. The 30-day runtime claim on the long-running-jobs page is marketing; the docs' own example tops out at 4 hours and no page states a ceiling, so a 730-hour timeout is untested.
